title: Ten sheep, two fields, how many ways?
_map: Splitting the flock (Y1–2). Big idea: number bonds, 10 can be split into two parts in set ways; the pattern; then 20.
_story: Steve built two fields but can't decide how to share 10 sheep. He finds every way, spots the pattern (one up, one down), catches Steve losing a sheep in its sums, then tries 20.
_stepChain: counting → 10 sheep, two fields → split them any way → every split still makes 10 → named number bonds → the pattern → Steve's mistake (6 and 3) → 20 sheep

talk.ask: How many ways can 10 sheep go into two fields?
talk.goodAnswer: 11 ways, from 0 and 10 up to 10 and 0. Every way still makes 10.

talk.ask: When one field gets one more sheep, what happens to the other one?
talk.goodAnswer: it gets one fewer, so the total stays 10.

handsOn: Take 10 Lego bricks and two bowls. Find every way to share them, and line the ways up in order: 0 and 10, 1 and 9 … What pattern do you see?

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Look, Ismaeel! I built two fields, full of yummy grass. And I've got 10 sheep. Baa! But how many should go in each field? I can't decide! Will you help me try different ways?
Pick how many sheep go into the first field, then tap the hammer. The rest trot into the other field. How many different ways can you find?
Here's something cool. Every way still makes 10 sheep! 4 and 6. 7 and 3. Even 0 and 10! Two numbers that make 10 together have a name. They're called number bonds.
Watch this pattern. One sheep hops from this field to that one. Hop! One field gets one more. The other gets one fewer. So altogether? Still 10!

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: I've got it! I put 6 sheep in the first field, and 3 sheep in the other field. That's all 10 sheep! Easy!

question.onRight: Yes, you caught him! 6 and 3 only make 9. One sheep is missing!

0.mistake: didn't check that the two parts add back up to 10
0.hint: Count them up: 6, then 3 more. Do you get to 10?
0.say: Let's count on from 6 together: 7, 8, 9. Only 9! One sheep is still wandering off somewhere! With 6 in the first field, the other field needs 4.

question.reveal: 6 and 4 make 10. Steve forgot a sheep! Baa!

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Oops! Thanks, Ismaeel. Guess what? More sheep are coming. 20 of them!

question.prompt: How many ways can 20 sheep go into two fields? Make a guess!
question.reveal: 21 ways! From 0 and 20, all the way to 20 and 0. 10 sheep had 11 ways. 20 sheep have 21 ways. Always one more than the number of sheep!

rule.text: Split 10 any way: the parts still make 10.
rule.ask: However you split the sheep, what stays the same? Say it out loud! Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: However you split 10, the two parts still make 10. Those pairs are called number bonds.

bonus.prompt: Bonus! What if there were three fields? Guess how many ways 10 sheep could go!
bonus.reveal: 66 ways! One more field makes loads more ways. Mathematicians love puzzles like this!
